chose: the genetics frame predicts two instruments coherence lacks: (1) LOCALIZED growth-without-anchoring — a component whose mass grows while its claim count stays flat is the software analogue of a tumor (local fitness, global lethality), which the existing repo-wide novelty-vs-anchor advisory cannot localize; (2) GERMLINE vs SOMATIC gate stratification — an edit to the harness propagates to every consumer while an edit to a consumer dies with it, so harness-side gates should be strictly stronger than consumer-side ones, and an unpinned consumer (the posthog/context-mill pattern: one release reshapes the whole fleet's field) is germline editing without a checkpoint
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
both are real and cheap: (1) is mass dims joined against per-component claim counts, already both in status.json; (2) is a policy plus a release-side check that no consumer resolves a floating ref
(1) is noise on a young repo where mass legitimately outruns claims during exploration, and would fire constantly on any greenfield component
discriminatedBy: compute mass-delta vs claim-delta per component over the last N commits on hoist and this repo; if the ratio flags components a human agrees are under-anchored (and stays quiet on ones they agree are fine), it is an instrument; if it flags everything young, it needs a maturity gate before it can ship

chose: PREMISE ROT: a journaled decision can state a premise that later work invalidates, and nothing in the harness detects it. Found live in hoist: app.spec.md filed the paths invariants at root because 'the feature has no single node — the store and the wire composition live in the Patient DO and worker.ts respectively'; the capability extraction moved the store, tools and declaration into shared/paths, dissolving that premise, and the decision now reads as current guidance with a false reason. The journal is append-only and self-correcting for RETRACTED decisions, but has no mechanism for decisions whose stated reason silently expired
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes

a real and detectable advisory class: many premises name structural facts a graph already holds (a file path, 'lives in X', 'has no single node', 'confined to Y', a symbol name) — a scanner could extract path/symbol-shaped tokens from --because text and flag entries whose referents no longer exist or moved
undetectable in general: most premises are semantic, not structural, and a scanner that only catches path-shaped ones would give false confidence that the rest were checked
discriminatedBy: extract path/symbol tokens from every --because in hoist's 160-entry journal, resolve each against the current graph, and hand-classify the hits: if a meaningful fraction are genuinely rotted (not just moved-but-equivalent), the advisory is real; if it is mostly noise or only ever finds the one case we already know, it is not worth building

chose: the README names all three events the generated hook block carries, and says what SessionStart is FOR
over: documenting SubagentStart alone, as it stood
waiting to rewrite the whole hooks section with tick-resolution doctrine
because: the tool's own printHooks emits SubagentStart, SessionStart and SubagentStop, and the code handles SessionStart identically to SubagentStart — but the README mentioned SessionStart ZERO times, so a reader who followed the docs and then ran 'coherence hooks' got back a block containing an event the documentation never explained. A doc that under-describes its own generated output is the same defect class as a stale claim: the reader stops inferring and stops at the wrong answer. The tick-resolution doctrine (which gate belongs at which tick) is deliberately NOT written here — that is a live experiment, and doctrine written ahead of its evidence is the thing this harness exists to prevent

chose: claims will carry PROVENANCE — what evidence produced them — because an incident-born claim and a design-conjectured one are currently indistinguishable once written
over: leaving provenance to ## why prose, where it is unparseable and optional
blocking claims that cite no evidence (design-born invariants are legitimate — hoist's tier-1 patient fold was designed, never observed failing)
because: the harness demands a claim PROVE it fires (probe double-entry, refutations) and is silent on where the claim CAME FROM. A claim generalized from an observed failure is a recording of an experiment that already ran; a claim conjectured from a theory is a hypothesis. Both are worth having and they should not be trusted equally — but today they wear the same grammar, the same oracle and the same tier, so the never-red advisory cannot tell an invariant that has never fired because it is perfect from one that has never fired because it was never grounded. That is the novice-judgment failure mode with a mechanical fix: make the empirical path the CHEAPEST path rather than a discipline someone remembers

config.test = node --test with a glob, which is WORSE than nothing: with more than one file argument node reports FILE-level counts and --test-name-pattern stops being legible, so a real name and a name that exists nowhere produce byte-identical passing output
via test, which the live-domain meta-oracle correctly rejects for unit oracles that iterate no live SSOT
because: a claim with no oracle checks only that its symbol exists in the graph (phrasebook.ts:259) — the harness demanded of hoist exactly what it was not doing itself. The shim resolves a test name to its owning file and runs that file ALONE, which is also the only honest execution mode here: two suites fail under node's parallel multi-file mode while passing in isolation. Proven, not asserted: the same mutation that was green now reds by name
